result:
Commit `be2e8c142ec2cc2b0eccaa6a8335b799ed493895` on `w1/W1-30` holds the round 7 cases: five new cases in `tests/acceptance/W1-30/test_w1_30_check_blocks.py` and a "Round 7" part in the README.

## Counts

The full run (`env -u PYTHONPATH python3 -m pytest tests/acceptance/W1-30 -q -p no:cacheprovider -rs`, 4 min 49 s) gave 204 cases in 18 files: 200 passed, 4 failed, none skipped. The 199 earlier cases are all green; of the five new ones, one is green and four are red.

## Blocking state taken

The W1-26 README states only one blocking state in words ("Hard-block RED: `ok: false`, exit 3"), so I wrote the one you named. Its behaviour is fixed by W1-26's own cases (`test_w1_26_dec436.py`, DEC-436), not by the README.

The project declares two checks of its own: `readme-present`, and `feature-present` in the family `licence hygiene`, which is none of the runner's families. Each case runs `gov check --json` at the commit being closed and fails there unless:
- the exit code is 3 and `ok` is false;
- no hard-block check is red;
- `feature-present` is GREEN;
- the families the runner reports RED are exactly `licence hygiene`.

The family the answer must name is read from the runner's answer, not written into the case.

## Cases and red reasons

| Case | Result | What `gov close` did |
|---|---|---|
| `test_a_close_is_refused_where_gov_check_blocks_and_no_hard_block_check_is_red[hard-block]` | red | closed the ticket (exit 0, `ok: true`) although `gov check` blocks |
| `…[warning]` (the passing check declared at warning; the family is still RED) | red | the same |
| `test_a_refusal_where_gov_check_blocks_is_counted` | red | closed the ticket; nothing refused, so nothing counted |
| `test_a_refusal_where_gov_check_blocks_opens_a_dependent_repair_ticket` | red | closed the ticket; no repair ticket |
| `test_the_same_ticket_closes_where_gov_check_does_not_block` | green | closed, as it should: same project, ticket and check, declared in `graph integrity`; `gov check` exits 0 with no check and no family red |

All four red cases fail at the close itself ("gov close was not refused"), not at the fixture.

## Notes

- **Second form added:** the refusal case runs in two forms (the passing check declared hard-block, and declared warning). The warning form is my addition within the same state.
- **Not written:** a hard-block policy key of the path map that no check covers. In the runner's code this appears as a check entry of its own (`policy-<key>`, hard-block, RED), so it falls under "a hard-block check is red". I did not run it.
- **Left untouched:** `tests/acceptance/W1-30/explore_tmp.py` (empty, untracked before this session) and `docs/checkpoints/`; neither is in the commit.
